chapter: Cab Calloway, Haiti and Sarah Vaughan
title: Recording the Haitian drummers in New York
summary: Budd arranges a record date with Ti-Roro and other Haitian drummers, Hilton Jefferson, Hinton and Pemberton.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Huh. I remember I met him through you.
I think Jeff was on that recording date too.
Bill Pemberton was on that date. You remember?

And they had brought up Ti-Ro-Ro, which is one of the greatest drummers for Haiti. They say he's the greatest drummer because they have six different rites there, like the Bushmen and all, and he can play in the language of all of their rites, the ceremonies. And that's why they call him the greatest drummer. They had another great drummer named T. Marcel. But then he brought his few key men, drummers, to the United States -- Bill Hinton, Hilton Jefferson and myself, Bill Pemberton and all, and I wrote the arrangements and everything. And we made a record
